summary: Middle-aged/older man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (EF <20%) s/p HeartMate II LVAD, listed status 1A(b) for heart transplant, admitted after a single ICD shock while on a fishing trip. Device interrogation showed one shock plus >20 VT episodes aborted by ATP despite maximal antiarrhythmic therapy (quinidine, mexiletine, metoprolol); he underwent a repeat left stellate ganglion block with no further VT on telemetry. He also had a week of increased lower extremity edema with JVD 14 cm on admission, managed by diuretic adjustment (torsemide held then resumed), discharged near-euvolemic at 120.4 kg.
most_likely: Refractory ventricular tachycardia in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with LVAD

differential.diagnosis: Refractory ventricular tachycardia with appropriate ICD shock
supporting_evidence: Chief complaint: ICD shock
Interrogation: one shock, >20 VT episodes aborted by ATP
Left stellate ganglion block performed this admission
Prior admission principal ICD-10 I472 for same problem
opposing_evidence: No VT recorded on telemetry after block
differential.reasoning: The entire admission was driven by documented recurrent VT despite maximal antiarrhythmic therapy, requiring an invasive sympathetic block; this is the billable principal disease rather than the shock event.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure, NYHA class III/stage D
supporting_evidence: Stage D heart failure, LVEF <20% on TTE
JVD 14 cm and 2+ bilateral pitting edema on admission
Torsemide dose escalated at home then re-titrated inpatient
opposing_evidence: Lungs clear, no crackles, room air saturation 97-99%
differential.reasoning: Actively managed volume overload with diuretic titration and daily weights makes chronic systolic HF a strongly supported concurrent diagnosis, though the acute driver was arrhythmia.

differential.diagnosis: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with biventricular dysfunction
supporting_evidence: TTE: severe biventricular dilation, severe global hypokinesis
Longstanding EF 10-20% non-ischemic DCM documented
Moderate-severe MR, moderate TR, mild-moderate AR
differential.reasoning: Underlying substrate for both VT and heart failure, objectively confirmed on this admission's echocardiogram.

differential.diagnosis: Presence of left ventricular assist device (HeartMate II)
supporting_evidence: LVAD flow 5.3-6.4, speed 9400, PI 3.1-4.4 documented daily
Driveline managed by VAD team
Doppler-only blood pressures
differential.reasoning: Device status materially affected management (anticoagulation, Doppler BP, driveline care) and is a codable status condition for this stay.

differential.diagnosis: Acute on chronic volume overload (decompensated right heart failure)
supporting_evidence: One week of increased lower extremity edema before shock
JVD 14 cm improving to 10 cm; weight 120.4 kg at discharge
Home torsemide increased to 30 mg then back-titrated
opposing_evidence: Clinician documented patient appeared relatively euvolemic
differential.reasoning: Congestive signs were present and diuretics adjusted, but the note explicitly downplays overload, so this ranks as a contributory rather than principal issue.

differential.diagnosis: Horner syndrome following stellate ganglion block
supporting_evidence: Transitional issue: Horner Syndrome was induced after block
No hematoma or respiratory compromise at injection site
opposing_evidence: Expected physiologic effect of the procedure, not an adverse event
differential.reasoning: Documented post-procedure finding worth capturing, though it is an anticipated consequence of a successful sympathetic block.

differential.diagnosis: Supratherapeutic INR on long-term warfarin anticoagulation
supporting_evidence: INR 3.3, PT 36.9, PTT 44.2 on labs
Warfarin regimen adjusted for discharge
Invasive neck block performed while anticoagulated
differential.reasoning: INR modestly above typical target with a periprocedural bleeding risk; clinically silent, so low-moderate score.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease with mild creatinine elevation
supporting_evidence: Creatinine 1.4 on admission, BUN 31 then 25
Prior admissions coded N189 and repeated AKI
Torsemide held for concern of overdiuresis
opposing_evidence: Creatinine improved to 1.2 at discharge, near baseline
differential.reasoning: Baseline renal impairment with cardiorenal sensitivity influenced diuretic dosing, but no acute kidney injury was declared this stay.

supporting_evidence: Longstanding T2DM in past medical history
Glucose 105-118 during stay
opposing_evidence: No diabetes medications listed on current admission med list
differential.reasoning: Stable chronic comorbidity with mild hyperglycemia; codable background condition only.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic tophaceous gout on urate-lowering therapy
supporting_evidence: Continued colchicine 0.6 mg QOD and febuxostat 80 mg daily
Tophaceous gout in PMH and prior ICD coding
opposing_evidence: No acute flare documented this admission
differential.reasoning: Chronic condition actively medicated but clinically quiescent during this stay.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Inappropriate ICD shock due to atrial arrhythmia or lead malfunction
rule_outs.why: Interrogation confirmed true VT episodes with ATP therapy, making the shock appropriate.
No chest pain, no troponin abnormality documented, known non-ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Stable LVAD parameters, LDH only mildly elevated at 252 and falling to 203, hemoglobin stable.
Afebrile, WBC 5.3, driveline managed routinely without infection signs.
K 3.7-4.3 and Mg 1.8-2.2 with no significant derangement to explain VT.

uncertain_areas: Whether coders would list decompensated/chronic systolic heart failure rather than VT as principal
Degree to which volume overload triggered the arrhythmia (no BNP or right heart cath data)
Whether Horner syndrome was documented as a procedural complication or expected effect
Absence of current radiology limits assessment of pulmonary congestion
Atrial fibrillation status post AVJ ablation not addressed in current note
